title: Model Registry Intake: Clarify Version-lock Semantics and Compatibility Annotations for Community Weights
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Clarify requirements for onboarding new open/community model weights into the Model Registry. This ticket defines the exact semantics for 'version-lock' (what is locked: API contract, tokenizer, kv layout), the format and minimum fields for compatibility annotations (runtime features required, quantization tolerance, max-sequence assumptions), and the processing/validation steps that must run during intake. It also scopes what we consider an 'experimental' admission vs. 'production-ready' entry and documents fallback behavior for consumers of unpinned variants. Goal: remove ambiguity between PM, runtime, and engineering about what gets pinned, what metadata is required, and how runtime chooses compatible fallbacks when a variant is unpinned.
acceptance_criteria: A human-readable intake checklist exists and is stored in Confluence with required fields: model_family, commit_hash_or_release_tag, tokenizer_version, kv_cache_compat_hash, min_runtime_version, required_kernels, expected_max_seq_length, recommended_quantization_profiles, security_provenance (license + provenance link)
Pipeline validates incoming archive and emits structured compatibility warnings (missing tokenizer, missing KV layout hash) and blocks intake if critical fields are absent
Definition of 'version-lock' documented: pinning binds API schema + tokenizer + KV layout; runtime may still select quantization variants if 'soft-quant' annotation present
Compatibility annotation schema (JSON Schema) published in the repo and used by intake to populate the catalog entry

Runtime behavior specified: when a request asks for a pinned model and pinned version is unavailable, the system must return a 409 with a clear fallback suggestion; when a request asks for model family without pin, runtime will prefer 'stable' channel and degrade to 'best-effort' variant per the routing policy
Migration/playbook for unpinned -> pinned transition exists, including consumer notification, rolling pin window, and automated eval suite to gate pin decisions
Security review completed for handling community weights and documented exceptions if provenance is partial
decisions: Use a lightweight JSON Schema for compatibility annotations (stored next to model artifact) rather than an RDF/graph representation
Version-lock will be implemented as a three-field tuple recorded on the catalog entry: (api_schema_version, tokenizer_checksum, kv_layout_hash)
Intake pipeline will emit 'hard' and 'soft' validation levels: hard prevents admission, soft surfaces warnings in catalog UI
'experimental' label applied automatically when intake identifies missing >=2 recommended fields or if runtime profiling shows <70% parity with reference outputs
open_questions: What is the minimal acceptable provenance proof for community weights (source URL + commit vs signed artifact)?
Should we expose tokenizer versioning to end-users via API, or keep tokenizer differences an internal compatibility concern?
How should we encode runtime kernel requirements that are GPU-architecture specific (e.g., sm80-only kernels) in a way that the scheduler can consume?
Do we allow pinning to an S3 URI for private customers who want deterministic deployment, or require catalog-stored artifacts?
notes: Cross-functional session 2025-02-20: engineers asked for a strict KV layout hash because small KV differences have caused silent corruption at runtime; PM asked for tolerance window for tokenizer minor versions
Runtime team prototype suggests storing a per-model 'compat matrix' that maps runtime_version -> kernel_set -> expected_latency, but raising as follow-up ENG work
Design flagged UI space: catalog entry must surface 'compatibility signals' prominently (runtime-ready vs experimental vs unverified)
Legal suggested minimal license proof as link + SPDX tag; security wants provenance artifacts scanned for embedded keys
